findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose updates under concurrent cron runs
findings.body: Both the else branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) set retryCount to `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded at the start of the loop. If two cron instances run simultaneously (e.g., multiple deployments or a sharded scheduler), both may read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, causing one increment to be lost. This could allow more than two scheduling attempts or prevent deletion when the limit is exceeded. Use Prisma's atomic `increment: { retryCount: 1 }` instead.

findings.title: Deletion condition for retryCount > 1 lacks method filter
findings.body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler uses an OR condition: one branch deletes SMS reminders with scheduledDate in the past, the other deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of `method`. Currently only this SMS handler increments retryCount, but if the field is later used for email or WhatsApp reminders (or if existing data contains non-SMS rows with retryCount > 1), those unrelated reminders would be silently deleted. The second OR branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to restrict deletion to SMS reminders.

findings.title: No tests added for new retry count behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a new retryCount field and modifies deletion logic, but no tests are added to verify that a reminder is deleted after exactly two scheduling failures, that one failure does not cause deletion, or that successful scheduling does not reset/change retryCount. This is a critical behavior change in a cron job; without tests the risk of regression is high.

findings.title: DeleteMany on retryCount > 1 may cause sequential scan
findings.body: The new deletion condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is not covered by any existing index on WorkflowReminder. In a large deployment with many workflow reminders, this branch can trigger a sequential scan of the entire table on every cron run, degrading performance. An index on `retryCount` (or a partial index where retryCount > 1) should be considered.
